findings.summary: Clean designed evaluation sweep over 9 workflows with ZERO recovery actions triggered at 17:51:01-17:51:08Z on 2026-08-25. Per-workflow outcome snapshot (transcribed verbatim from the only raw witness): graph-loop.yml ACTIVE; physics-loop.yml latest completed run 32866107906 concluded success, no recovery; meta-sync.yml NO completed run to inspect (still zero completions lifetime at this timestamp); intel-loop.yml ACTIVE; product-loop.yml ACTIVE; product-beta-repair.yml NO completed run to inspect; runtime-loop.yml ACTIVE; cto-council.yml ACTIVE (the council chain that produced runs #8/#9 cancellations was in flight); frontier-research.yml NO completed run to inspect (first frontier dispatches had not yet completed). Corroborates the concurrency-burst timeline already distilled for council runs 32879459085/32879902647/32880285474.

Watchdog recovery policy executed is byte-equivalent to the version already transcribed in runs/32879908049.json (Ox Watchdog #74): rerun only on (a) runner-shutdown cancellation signatures, (b) explicit SPIDER_TRANSIENT_OX_EXHAUSTED marker, or (c) OpenCode/Ox + explicit transient-network regex; refuses blind retry when logs unreadable ('refusing blind retry'); never interrupts active runs ('does not interrupt potentially valid work'); no full-run replay fallback. No policy change between #74 and #75.

failure_signatures: None observed (conclusion=success, zero ::warning:: emissions). Known signatures this workflow can emit are documented in runs/32879908049.json and the workflow source at pinned head_sha.
research_opportunities: Orchestration-noise economics (already raised as IDEA in runs/32880942022.json): watchdog re-fires on every workflow_run completion; this instance and twin run 32880400040 fired 65s apart on the same head_sha during a multi-lane completion burst. A dedupe/debounce window or single-flight lock would remove pure-noise executions without touching the recovery function.
